title: Aviation Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
2. MOS 6604, Aviation Supply Operations Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC
AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation Supply Operations Officers are responsible for the
performance of aviation supply activities within Marine Aviation Logistics
Squadrons, Marine Aircraft Wings, Marine Corps Air Stations, and naval
expeditionary vessels. A high level of expertise is required to supervise
the execution of the various tasks encompassed within the wide spectrum of
aviation supply support. To be effective, Aviation Supply Operations
Officers must possess detailed and working knowledge of all Navy-developed
and sponsored aviation logistics information management systems, repairable
management programs, financial management programs, budgeting and accounting
functions, aviation inventory management systems and functions, and
warehousing operations. They must be skilled in working with a variety of
ashore and afloat automated systems such as relational supply (R-Supply), the
Naval Aviation Logistics Command Management Information Systems (NALCOMIS),
F-35 Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS), Supply Chain Management
(SCM), and other. They must be able to effectively use information extracted
from these systems to aid in supervision and control. In addition, Aviation
Supply Operations Officers must have detailed knowledge of all applicable
Navy Supply documents, forms, and publications and must be proficient in
working with Navy Supply afloat procedures, to include the support of
deployed aviation operations. Aviation Supply Operations Officers must
ensure that aviation supply operations support and sustain the unit's combat
readiness and enhance the unit's ability to perform its mission. They must
establish and maintain liaison with external agencies while providing or
obtaining support and reporting supply management indicators. A working
knowledge in acquisitions, life cycle logistics, and program management is
highly desirable for senior 6604 billets.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) This MOS may only be assigned to Warrant Officers who were
previously qualified in MOS 6672.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Marine Aviation Supply Officer Basic Qualification
Course (N42C0B3), Milton, FL.

        (2) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

        (3) Marines serving in billets coded with an additional skill
designator (ASD), as per the table of organization, must attain the
appropriate certification level through DAU within 24 months of billet
assignment.



                                           1-251                        Enclosure (1)
 1138                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (bn), Aviation Maintenance and Supply Training and Readiness
Program (AMSTRP).

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Transportation, Storage, and Distribution Managers 11-3071.

            (2) Logisticians 13-1081.

            (3) Financial Analysts and Advisors 13-2050.

            (4) Database Administrators 15-1242.

            (5) Industrial Engineers 17-2112.

            (6) Shipping, Receiving, and Inventory Clerks 43-5071.

            (7) Data Entry Clerks 43-9021.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Ground Supply Operations Officer, 3010.

            (2) Financial Management Resource Officer, 3408.

Aviation Supply Operations Officers are responsible for the performance of aviation supply activities within Marine Aviation Logistics Squadrons, Marine Aircraft Wings, Marine Corps Air Stations, and naval expeditionary vessels.
Supervise support staff and ensure proper execution of contracts.
A high level of expertise is required to supervise the execution of the various tasks encompassed within the wide spectrum of aviation supply support.
Manage activities related to strategic or tactical purchasing, material requirements planning, controlling inventory, warehousing, or receiving.

To be effective, Aviation Supply Operations Officers must possess detailed and working knowledge of all Navy-developed and sponsored aviation logistics information management systems, repairable management programs, financial management programs, budgeting and accounting functions, aviation inventory management systems and functions, and warehousing operations.
Provide technical support for robotic systems.

They must be skilled in working with a variety of ashore and afloat automated systems such as relational supply (R-Supply), the Naval Aviation Logistics Command Management Information Systems (NALCOMIS), F-35 Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS), Supply Chain Management (SCM), and other.
Establish system operating or training requirements to ensure optimized human-machine interfaces.
They must be able to effectively use information extracted from these systems to aid in supervision and control.
Procure, produce, and provide information on the safe operation of aircraft, such as flight planning publications, operations publications, charts and maps, or weather information.

In addition, Aviation Supply Operations Officers must have detailed knowledge of all applicable Navy Supply documents, forms, and publications and must be proficient in working with Navy Supply afloat procedures, to include the support of deployed aviation operations.
Coordinate with agencies, such as air traffic control, civil engineers, or command posts, to ensure support of airfield management activities.
Aviation Supply Operations Officers must ensure that aviation supply operations support and sustain the unit's combat readiness and enhance the unit's ability to perform its mission.
Monitor suppliers to ensure that they efficiently and effectively provide needed goods or services within budgetary limits.
They must establish and maintain liaison with external agencies while providing or obtaining support and reporting supply management indicators.
Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.
For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (bn), Aviation Maintenance and Supply Training and Readiness Program (AMSTRP).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
